title: fix(invites): flag existing members on the invite row before submit

criteria.behavior: While filling in an invite row, an email that belongs to an existing member of the current organization is flagged on that row itself (visible inline error/error styling on the email field) before any submission happens, in the organization settings invite dialog.
The signed-in user's own email address is treated the same as an existing member's email and is flagged on the row.

When any row contains an existing-member (or own) email, the batch submit control is unavailable and communicates a reason indicating that people who are already members must be removed; this applies both in the onboarding invite step and in the organization settings invite dialog. Per-row send controls are likewise unavailable for such a row.
The match against existing members' emails ignores letter case and surrounding whitespace, so e.g. ' Rose.Dawson@PostHog.com' is flagged when the member's email is rose.dawson@posthog.com.

The organization's member list is fetched when the invite form is opened so the check can work without the user having visited the members list first, and the own-email check still applies before that data has loaded.

A bulk invite request containing an existing member's email in any position is rejected as a bad request without creating or emailing any invite from that batch, including invites listed before the offending row.
The rejection is returned as a field-level validation error attributed to the target email with a stable, distinguishable code identifying the existing-member case (rather than a generic error).
An existing-member rejection of an invite submission is not sent to error tracking as an application exception, while other unexpected API failures on the same path still are.
If the server rejects a submission for an existing member that the client did not know about, the member data is refreshed so the offending row becomes flagged afterwards.
